sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Interesting! With the divider ON (horizontal at rows 48-50):
- LEFT, RIGHT: nothing moves.
- UP: a 'c' (charcoal) node appears at rows 60-62, cols 12-23! Wait, that's new — a charcoal piece appeared at the bottom? Actually, the 'c' node (60,12,62,23) appeared after UP and disappeared after DOWN. Hmm, that's weird. Maybe UP moved something, and a temporary object (a "shadow" of the player?) got rendered at the bottom? Or maybe UP moved the piece and the 'c' node is a partially hidden piece?
Wait, after UP: the bboxes of all 6 pieces are unchanged, plus a new 'c' node at rows 60-62, cols 12-23 (3 rows × 12 cols). After DOWN: the 'c' node disappears.
Hmm! Maybe UP/DOWN moves the black pieces (the "players")... no, the black bboxes are unchanged.
Maybe the 'c' node is a "ghost" of the player's mirror across the divider? The divider is at rows 48-50. The mirror of id4 (rows 21-32) across the divider center 49: row' = 98 - row → rows 66-77. Off the board. No.
Maybe 'c' is a piece that slid down... rows 60-62 is near the bottom edge (the black bar at row 63). Hmm.
Or maybe UP pressed the "player" piece up, and the player is hidden/overlapping? Let me look at the actual frame after UP — I should have saved it. Let me re-probe: press UP and inspect the full diff between before/after frames (all changed cells), not just the bboxes of the 6 pieces.
Also, the divider might be "off" right now (I pressed SPACE an even number of times? In this level I haven't pressed SPACE yet — the 4 actions were LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN). The divider line is visible in the image (the white dotted line at row 49). So the divider is ON.
Let me diff the before/after of UP in detail.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
import copy
f0 = current_frame
a0 = f0.ascii
action(['UP'])
f1 = current_frame
a1 = f1.ascii
l0=a0.split('\n'); l1=a1.split('\n')
diff=[]
for r in range(64):
    for c in range(64):
        if l0[r][c]!=l1[r][c]: diff.append((r,c,l0[r][c],l1[r][c]))
print("UP diff cells:", len(diff))
print("rows:", sorted(set(d[0] for d in diff)), "cols:", sorted(set(d[1] for d in diff)))
# summarize by color transition
from collections import Counter
print(Counter((d[2],d[3]) for d in diff))
action(['DOWN'])
print("after DOWN, c-node present?", any(n['color']=='c' and n['pixels']>10 for n in current_frame.segmentation['nodes']))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
